bib.title: RLHF Workflow: From Reward Modeling to Online RLHF

question: How can online iterative RLHF be reproduced with fully open-source data, using a proxy preference/reward model in place of human feedback?
hypothesis: Online iterative direct preference learning with a proxy preference model outperforms offline DPO, because fresh on-policy data mitigates out-of-distribution shift.
contributions: Open recipe for reward/preference model training from a mixture of open preference datasets
Online iterative DPO workflow with best-of-n vs worst-of-n exploration
State-of-the-art-for-size LLaMA-3-8B results on AlpacaEval-2, MT-Bench, Arena-Hard
Release of models, curated datasets and code guidebooks

method.summary: Train BT reward model and pairwise preference model from Llama-3-8B-Instruct on a mixture of open preference datasets; SFT LLaMA-3-8B; then run 3 iterations of DPO on data labelled by the BT reward model, where each iteration samples 16 responses per prompt and keeps best and worst as a pair.

datasets.name: Preference mix2 (HH-RLHF, SHP, HelpSteer, PKU-SafeRLHF-30K, UltraFeedback, UltraInteract, CodeUltraFeedback, Argilla-Math, OpenOrca, Capybara)
datasets.size: see Table 5; e.g. UltraFeedback 340025 pairs, HH-RLHF 115396 pairs
datasets.preprocessing: noisy samples, empty rounds, wrong labels and small-margin score pairs removed (roughly 10% deleted); SHP only score ratio >2, max 5 pairs per prompt

datasets.name: SFT data (ShareGPT, Evol-Instruct, SlimOrca, MathInstruct, Magicoder-Evol-Instruct, GPT4-LLM, OrcaMath, GPTeacher, UltraInteract)
RLHF prompt set (UltraFeedback, HelpSteer, OpenOrca, UltraInteract, Capybara, DIBT-10K)

models.name: BT reward model / pairwise preference model
models.architecture: Llama-3-8B-Instruct with linear scalar head (BT); next-token A/B prediction (preference)

other.note: Instruct checkpoint used because only it was available early

training.objective: BT reward: -E log sigma(r(x,aw)-r(x,al)); preference model: next-token A/B classification; SFT; DPO with eta=0.1 on best/worst-of-8 pairs
training.lr: SFT 2e-5; BT RM 2e-6; preference model 5e-6; iterative DPO peak 5e-7; offline DPO 5e-7
training.batch_size: SFT 32; BT RM 512; preference model 128; DPO 128 (global)
training.epochs: SFT 1; RM 1; preference model 1; DPO 2 epochs per iteration on all historical data; offline DPO 1
training.regularisation: DPO KL coefficient eta=0.1 (beta 0.1 in Table 7)

other.init_per_iteration: checkpoint from previous iteration as init, SFT model as reference (not restart from pi0)
other.length_penalty: r~ = r^ - lambda|a|, |a| characters, lambda=0.001 for the concise model
other.table7: per-device batch 2, grad accumulation 8, 2 epochs, beta 0.1

inference.temperature: 1.0 for n/2 responses and 0.7 for the other n/2
inference.samples: n=8 per prompt in Algorithm 2 (n/2 at each temperature); text also says 16 responses per prompt per iteration; best and worst by BT reward form a pair; pairs with identical responses dropped
inference.prompting: preference model input: [CONTEXT] {x} [RESPONSE A] {a1} [RESPONSE B] {a2}, label A or B, order randomised; P(a1>a2)=pA/(pA+pB)

results.claim: Online data theory: with batch size m = O~(d_e/eps^2), T = O~(d_e) iterations suffice for eps-optimal KL-regularised value (informal Theorem 2 of Xiong et al. 2023).

limits: Feedback is a proxy BT reward model, not humans; iterative RLHF heavily relies on preference-signal quality (Table 4).
Length bias amplified under iteration; length penalty is only a preliminary data-filtering fix and hurts Chat-Arena-Hard.
Preference model not used in the online loop; BT vs preference comparison left to future work; PPO not studied.
Benchmark results may be hacked/overfit; GPT-judge results depend on config (Remark 1).
Hardware, compute, seeds, SFT step counts and variance are not reported; single runs.
Reward model uses Llama-3-8B-Instruct while policy starts from base SFT.
Exploration by best/worst-of-8 is heuristic; theory is for linear rewards.
